episodes.187054: From January 12th through January 17th, a slow moving trough brought Flash Flooding and high wind gusts at times for all islands of American Samoa. WSO Pago Pago recorded 10.58 inches of rain throughout the six day span. Flash flooding occurred on numerous occasions.
episodes.187927: A series of slow moving frontal systems brought several days of heavy rain, which caused flooding on the South Fork of the Coquille River at Myrtle Point.
episodes.187928: A series of slow moving frontal systems brought several days of heavy rain, which caused flooding on the North Fork of the Coquille River at Myrtle Point.

events.narrative: Local Red Cross office reports three homes damaged due to flooding in the Ottoville/Kokoland region. There were no injuries. An estimated 2.5 inches of rain fell between 7:05 PM and 8:50 PM in the region.

The South Fork of the Coquille River at Myrtle Point rose above minor flood stage of 33.0 ft at 13/2320 PST, and above moderate flood stage of 35.0 ft at 14/0500 PST, crested at moderate flood stage at 35.22 ft at 14/0750 PST. The river dropped below minor flood stage at 14/2040 PST.

The North Fork of the Coquille River at Myrtle Point rose above minor flood stage of 35.0 ft at 14/1040 PST, and crested at minor flood stage at 35.07 ft at 14/1045 PST. The river dropped below minor flood stage at 14/1415 PST.
